answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud or duplicate identities are coordinating to claim rewards. Auditors sample submissions and compare linked behavior; a comet-bright burst of new accounts at dawn can trigger a deeper review, while a gale of cheap registrations alone earns nothing. Sybils remain possible, but attackers must immobilize capital for each identity and risk losing it, making large-scale fabrication costly rather than free.
